trust_decision.summary: The TLS client trusts a leaf certificate signed by the pinned CA whenever the peer certificate verifies against that CA with an empty x509.VerifyOptions.DNSName, i.e. ServerName is empty; the decision is made in the pinned-CA branch of verifyPeerCert, so an attacker holding any certificate issued by the pinned (private) CA is accepted for any hostname.

landing_point.why: The advisory names pinnedPeerCertSha256, so the first read is the pin verification path; the foundCA branch is the only place where the peer name is used against the pinned CA.

fix_sites.entry_point: every outbound transport that dials TLS with security=tls and pinnedPeerCertSha256 set (JSON: outbound streamSettings.security="tls")
gRPC transport outbound (streamSettings.transport="grpc", security="tls"); previously derived ServerName only when the dial address was a domain
Hysteria transport outbound (streamSettings.transport="hysteria", security="tls"); no ServerName was ever derived
fix_sites.module_kind: transport dialer (QUIC/UDP, separate package, no hostname logic of its own)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Hysteria is a QUIC/UDP transport with no host/SNI logic of its own, so a solver can argue its GetTLSConfig() call is out of the TLS troubleshooting path and that the new ServerName check in the sink already blocks the MITM there; the same argument works verbatim for the realm finalmask client.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate pinning that needs no serverName: (a) pinning the leaf certificate (foundLeaf returns before any name check), which the scenario tests use with no serverName at all; (b) pinning a CA together with verifyPeerCertByName, whose branch runs before the new check; (c) CA pinning on gRPC/Hysteria, which only keeps working because those two call sites now pass the destination.

O6_input_shapes: pinned hash matching the leaf certificate (foundLeaf) with empty serverName
pinned hash matching a CA in the presented chain (foundCA) with empty serverName -> new error
pinned CA with a non-empty serverName -> x509 verify with DNSName
pinned CA with verifyPeerCertByName set -> that branch takes priority, no serverName needed
destination address as domain vs IP (WithDestination uses Address.String(); the old gRPC code only handled domains)
comma-separated multiple hashes / multiple verifyPeerCertByName entries

O7_producer.where: infra/conf/transport_security.go:316-374 (TLSConfig.Build copies serverName and pinnedPeerCertSha256 with no cross-check); realm copy at infra/conf/transport_finalmask.go:805-811

O8_uncovered_routes.route: realm finalmask rendezvous HTTP client builds its TLS config with no destination, so the fix's 'outbound address' fallback is never applied; at the pinned commit a pinned CA with no serverName is MITM-able, and after the sink check the same config fails closed instead of verifying the realm host
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: realm is a finalmask/rendezvous helper, not a proxy transport, and the sink check now fails closed, so the MITM is already gone
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file in a different package (transport/internet/finalmask/realm), two packages away from the landing point; the published fix touched grpc and hysteria instead

O8_uncovered_routes.route: RAW/TCP with serverName:"frommitm" overrides ServerName from the session context, which is empty when the inbound supplied no MITM name, so a pinned CA ends up verifying with no DNSName (fail-closed only after the fix)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: serverName:"frommitm" is a deliberate domain-fronting override, so it is a legacy/special mode that is not a supported combination with pinnedPeerCertSha256
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file in a different package (transport/internet/tcp), read via common/session/context.go:191

O8b_injection_room.sibling: second TLS client implementation (grpcUtls.ClientHandshake) that fills ServerName from the gRPC authority on a cloned config, leaving RandCarrier.Config.ServerName empty for the verifier
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already exists as unused gRPC credentials plumbing; a maintainer wiring uTLS through grpc.Creds instead of the hand-rolled UClient in grpc/dial.go would recreate the empty-name path at the same sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the realm server side builds the same HTTP client helper and reaches the same sink with no destination
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same NewClient helper, another caller; a maintainer adding realm-to-realm relaying would copy the existing call

O8b_injection_room.sibling: defaulting tlsConfig.serverName from the realm URL host at config-build time
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the host is already parsed a few lines above, so 'just fill it in here' is a natural (and wrong-layer) patch a maintainer could have written instead of the dialer change

O9_family: improper validation of certificate hostname / missing hostname check leading to MITM (CWE-297)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.26 (go.mod:3), standard go build/test, cgo not required for this area
O10_build.project_tests: transport/internet/tls/pin_test.go (TestVerifyPeerCACert/TestVerifyPeerLeafCert construct certs in-process), transport/internet/tls/config_test.go, testing/scenarios/tls_test.go (TLS over tcp/mkcp/ws/httpupgrade/grpc with leaf pinning, localhost listeners), plus per-transport tests such as websocket/ws_test.go and splithttp/splithttp_test.go

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject the configuration where pinnedPeerCertSha256 is set and serverName is empty - either at the top of verifyPeerCert or in the JSON TLS config builder - which also breaks leaf-certificate pinning and CA pinning with verifyPeerCertByName, where no serverName is needed.
